blocks.prompt: 5. The vertices of a triangle are \(A(2, -1)\), \(B(4, 3)\) and \(C(6, -1)\). Find the equations of altitudes and show that they are concurrent.
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do kaam hain: teeno altitudes ki equations nikalna, aur phir saabit karna ke woh ek hi point par milte hain.
Har altitude ek vertex se guzarta hai aur samne wali side par perpendicular hota hai, is liye har dafa point aur perpendicular slope chahiye.
Ek side horizontal hai (dono siron ka \(y = -1\)); wahan altitude vertical banega, us ka khayal rakhna hai.
Plan: sides ki slopes, teen point-slope equations, phir Theorem 3 ka determinant.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(2, -1)\), \(B(4, 3)\), \(C(6, -1)\).
Maloom karna: altitudes, aur saabit karna ke woh concurrent hain.
Tareeqa: perpendicular slope aur point-slope form (Example 8 ki tarah), phir Theorem 3.
Example 8 mein kitab ne bilkul yahi tareeqa istemal kiya tha: pehle side ki slope, phir us ka negative reciprocal, phir vertex se point-slope form. Hum har altitude ke liye yahi teen qadam dohrayenge.

\(A\) se altitude (\(BC\) par perpendicular)
\[m_{BC} = \dfrac{-1 - 3}{6 - 4} = -2\]
\[m = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[y + 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}(x - 2)\]
\[x - 2y - 4 = 0 \;\ldots(i)\]
Kyun: \(-2\) ka negative reciprocal \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai; phir \(A(2, -1)\) se point-slope form aur 2 se multiply: \(2y + 2 = x - 2\).
Dhyan dein: point-slope form mein A ka y-coordinate minus ek hai, is liye y - (-1) = y + 1 likha; yahan sign ki ghalti bahut aam hai.

\(B\) se altitude (\(CA\) par perpendicular)
\[m_{CA} = \dfrac{-1 - (-1)}{6 - 2} = 0\]
\(CA\) horizontal hai (\(y = -1\)), is liye \(B\) se altitude vertical hai:
\[x = 4 \;\text{ or }\; x - 4 = 0 \;\ldots(ii)\]
Kyun: horizontal line par perpendicular line vertical hoti hai, jis ki slope undefined hai. Yahan \(-\frac{1}{m}\) wala formula kaam nahi karta kyunke \(m = 0\) hai.
Dhyan dein: \(-\frac{1}{0}\) likh dena ghalat hai; seedha socho ke vertical line \(B\) se guzre to \(x = 4\).

\(C\) se altitude (\(AB\) par perpendicular)
\[m_{AB} = \dfrac{3 + 1}{4 - 2} = 2\]
\[m = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[y + 1 = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 6)\]
\[x + 2y - 4 = 0 \;\ldots(iii)\]
Kyun: \(2\) ka negative reciprocal \(-\frac{1}{2}\); \(C(6, -1)\) se point-slope form: \(2y + 2 = -x + 6\).

Concurrent saabit karein (Theorem 3)
\[\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 2 & -4 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(0 + 8) + 2(-4 + 4) - 4(2 - 0)\]
\[= 8 + 0 - 8 = 0\]
Kyun: rows (i), (ii), (iii) ke coefficients hain ((ii) ke liye \(1, 0, -4\)). Determinant zero hai (column 1 aur column 3 proportional hain, column 3 = \(-4\) guna column 1), aur koi do altitudes parallel nahi, is liye concurrent hain.
Ek aur nazar se dekhein: teeno equations mein \(x\) ka coefficient 1 aur constant \(-4\) hai; sirf \(y\) ka coefficient \(-2\), \(0\), \(2\) badal raha hai. Isi liye \(x = 4, y = 0\) teeno ko foran poora kar deta hai.

Tasdeeq: point of concurrency
(ii) se \(x = 4\); (i) mein: \(4 - 2y - 4 = 0\), yani \(y = 0\). (iii) mein: \(4 + 0 - 4 = 0\). Teeno \((4, 0)\) se guzarte hain. Equations answer key (number 6) se milti hain.
Altitudes ka yeh common point orthocentre kehlata hai. Is triangle mein AB aur BC ki slopes 2 aur minus 2 hain, yani triangle do barabar sides wala (isosceles) hai, aur orthocentre bilkul B ke neeche wali seedhi line par aaya.
blocks.final_answer: Altitudes: \(x - 2y - 4 = 0\) (from \(A\)), \(x - 4 = 0\) (from \(B\)), \(x + 2y - 4 = 0\) (from \(C\)); determinant \(= 0\), so they are concurrent, meeting at \((4, 0)\).
